messages:
maria-cs: Hey — AcmeCorp escalated. Their /v1/rerank responses show scores like -12.3, -0.98, 0.12. They expected 0..1 probabilities. Any quick explanation I can give?

jordan-ml: Those are raw model scores (logits / dot products). Not probabilities. Negative values are fine. Suggest: tell them to softmax the array if they need probabilities.

maria-cs: Got it. Can you give a tiny snippet I can paste back? Also asking what caused such a wide range (why -12 is possible).

jordan-ml: Paste this: ```python
import numpy as np
s = np.array([-12.345, -0.987, 0.123])
probs = np.exp(s - s.max()) / np.exp(s - s.max()).sum()
print(probs)  # sums to 1, all in 0..1
```
Explain: logits are unbounded; magnitude depends on model scale / vector norms / dot-product magnitude. Negative numbers simply mean lower relative affinity.

akash-eng: Can you share the request id and body? I want to repro locally. Also which model they used.

maria-cs: Request id req_20260317_01. Body (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-re-rank-1",
  "query": "how to reset password",
  "candidates": ["reset password via settings","contact support","forgot password link"],
  "top_k": 5
}
```
Response sample:```json
{
  "candidates": ["reset password via settings","forgot password link","contact support"],
  "scores": [-12.345, -0.987, 0.123]
}
```
Customer: "are these broken? why negative?"

jordan-ml: Not broken. Two quick consumer-friendly lines you can send: 1) "The rerank scores are raw model scores (not probabilities) and can be negative or >1; they indicate relative preference among candidates." 2) "If you need them as probabilities, apply softmax across the candidate list."

noah-product: Long term this is confusing. Two product asks: 1) KB article next to the rerank API docs that explains score semantics + example conversions; 2) consider optional response field or query param (normalize_scores=true) that returns probabilities for convenience (opt-in to avoid breaking existing users).

akash-eng: Reproduced with req_20260317_01 against rwd-re-rank-1 — we return unnormalized logits. Short-term: I'll add a note to the API reference and push a small SDK helper (normalize_scores) that wraps softmax and logs a warning if users assume 0..1. ETA SDK patch: 3 days. API change: requires spec, ~2 sprints.

support-bot: Created ticket TCK-5873 for AcmeCorp (assigned akash-eng). Priority P2. https://tickets.internal/TCK-5873

maria-cs: I sent jordan's snippet and a short explanation to the customer. They accepted softmax workaround but want a KB link they can cite. I drafted a KB and linked it from the ticket.

jordan-ml: KB bullets for reference: 
- "score": raw model output (logit/dot-product), unbounded and relative.
- To convert to a probability distribution across candidates, apply softmax.
- If you want per-item 0..1 independent scores, apply a sigmoid/logistic to each score but note they won't sum to 1 and are not a probability distribution over candidates.
- SDKs will include a helper: normalize_scores(scores, method='softmax')

noah-product: Maria, ask Acme whether they prefer a distribution (sums to 1) or independent 0..1 relevance scores. We should capture the most common preference in KB.

maria-cs: Will do. Marking this resolved on our side for now; will reopen if they ask for an API normalization flag. KB draft saved to internal confluence. :thumbsup:

akash-eng: I'll push the SDK helper PR today and add a runtime hint in the client when scores fall outside 0..1 so users aren't surprised.

maria-cs: Thanks all. Closing the loop unless Acme asks to reopen.
